newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market thin at $70 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market thin at $70 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Friday were slow at $70.00 per cwt, unchanged from this week's sales, feedlot sources said.
Under 500 head were reported sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma region and close to 1,500 sold in Kansas.

Most of this week's sales took place Thursday, with a moderate number of cattle shipped Friday morning in Kansas to packers who were short on live inventories, the feedlot sources said. Shipment from Panhandle feedlots ranged from a few days to the normal pick up of seven days.
Tight supplies of market-ready cattle offset potential weakness from lower beef prices and kept feedlot cattle prices unchanged from a week ago, the feedlot sources said.
Beef prices were lower for the week, but rebounded slightly Friday as demand for choice beef increased.
Choice beef supplies were limited by the large number of unfinished cattle being marketed at feedlots and grading mostly select, market sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.41 to $0.78 for choice and unchanged to up $0.05 for select, USDA said. Heavyweight choice beef at $104.79 was off $0.67 since Friday.
